- Frontend framework: React 19
- Meta-framework: Next.js 16
- Styling: Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn/ui
- State / data fetching: TanStack Query, Zustand
- Backend framework: Fastify
- Backend language: Node.js + TypeScript
- Database: PostgreSQL
- ORM / query builder: Prisma 6
- Authentication: Auth.js (NextAuth)
- Jobs / queues: None
- File storage: None
- Realtime: None
- AI / ML: None
- Testing: Vitest, Playwright
- Deployment target: Vercel
- Mobile (optional): Web only

Build a modern landing page for a saas company

Rules:

  • Output the patched files in full — do not emit diffs.

FROM node:22-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

FROM node:22-alpine AS runner
WORKDIR /app
ENV NODE_ENV=production
COPY --from=builder /app/package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --omit=dev
COPY --from=builder /app/dist ./dist
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "dist/server.js"]

    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    env_file:

    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "--spider", "-q", "http://localhost:3000/health"]
      interval: 15s

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

if [[ ! -f .env ]]; then
  echo "Missing .env file. Copy .env.example to .env and configure values."
  exit 1
fi

docker compose pull || true
docker compose build --pull
docker compose up -d --remove-orphans
docker compose ps
echo "Deployment complete."

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

if (-not (Test-Path .env)) {
  Write-Error "Missing .env file. Copy .env.example to .env and configure values."
}

docker compose pull
docker compose build --pull
docker compose up -d --remove-orphans
docker compose ps
Write-Host "Deployment complete."

#!/usr/bin/env bash

required=("NODE_ENV" "PORT")
missing=0
for name in "${required[@]}"; do
  if [[ -z "${!name:-}" ]]; then
    echo "Missing required env var: ${name}"
    missing=1
  fi
done

if [[ ${missing} -ne 0 ]]; then
  exit 1
fi
echo "Environment validation passed."

name: Deploy

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    branches: ["main"]

jobs:
  build-and-publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
      - name: Login to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - name: Build and push
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          push: true
          tags: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:latest
      - name: Deployment note
        run: echo "Image published. Add environment-specific deploy step (Kubernetes, ECS, or VM)."

# Design System (DO NOT EDIT)

Every UI file in this project MUST follow these rules. The build pipeline
sanitises violations and the QA agent flags any deviation as critical.

## Allowed colour classes (semantic, themed)

- Surfaces: `bg-background`, `bg-card`, `bg-popover`, `bg-muted`, `bg-accent`
- Text: `text-foreground`, `text-card-foreground`, `text-popover-foreground`,
  `text-muted-foreground`, `text-accent-foreground`
- Brand: `bg-primary`, `text-primary`, `text-primary-foreground`,
  `bg-secondary`, `text-secondary`, `text-secondary-foreground`
- Status: `bg-destructive`, `text-destructive`, `text-destructive-foreground`
- Borders/rings: `border-border`, `border-input`, `ring-ring`, `ring-primary`
- Opacity modifiers: `/10 /20 /50 /80 /90` (e.g. `bg-primary/10`)

Tailwind palette colours (`bg-green-500`, etc.) are allowed ONLY inside
`Badge` / `Alert` variants for static status indicators.

## Banned class patterns

- Invented camelCase tokens: `bg-cardBackground`, `text-textPrimary`,
  `border-borderColor`, `bg-mainBg`, `text-headingColor` — these do not
  exist and produce invisible elements.
- Raw hex / rgb anywhere in className or style.
- Arbitrary values like `p-[13px]` or `w-[742px]` outside hero / chart code.

## Allowed primitives (import, never redefine)

```ts
import { Button, Input, Textarea, Select, Card, CardHeader, CardTitle,
  CardDescription, CardContent, CardFooter, Badge, Alert, AlertTitle,
  AlertDescription, Dialog, DialogTrigger, DialogContent, DialogHeader,
  DialogTitle, DialogDescription, DialogFooter, Tabs, TabsList, TabsTrigger,
  TabsContent, Separator, Avatar, AvatarImage, AvatarFallback, Spinner,
  Skeleton, EmptyState, AppShell, PageHeader, ToastProvider, useToast
} from '@/components/ui';
import { cn } from '@/lib/cn';
```

## Layout template

- Multi-page / dashboard apps wrap pages in `<AppShell>`.
- Single-page marketing sites use a hero + sections layout but every
  block lives inside `max-w-screen-2xl mx-auto` and uses `Card` for
  panels.
- Page intro: `<PageHeader title=… description=… actions=… />`.
- Spacing scale: `gap-4` between siblings, `gap-6` between sections,
  `gap-8` between major regions.

## Theme

`globals.css` ships `:root` (light) + `.dark` blocks; `<html>` has
`className="dark"` by default. Use semantic tokens — never fork into
a "dark variant" branch.

spec.oneLiner: A modern, conversion-focused landing page for a SaaS company, showcasing features, testimonials, pricing, and a clear call-to-action.
spec.summary: Nimbus SaaS Landing is a responsive, visually engaging landing page designed for SaaS companies to attract, inform, and convert visitors. It highlights the product’s value proposition, core features, customer testimonials, and pricing plans, culminating in a prominent call-to-action for sign-ups or demos. The page is optimized for performance, accessibility, and SEO, and leverages a modern React/Next.js stack with shadcn/ui primitives and Tailwind CSS v4.
targetUsers: SaaS founders seeking to launch or relaunch their product’s web presence
Marketing teams aiming to increase sign-ups or demo requests
Investors or partners researching the company
spec.expandedPrompt: Nimbus SaaS Landing is a single-page web application designed to serve as the primary marketing and conversion funnel for a SaaS product. The landing page is structured to guide visitors through a compelling narrative: it opens with a hero section that succinctly communicates the product’s unique value proposition and offers a clear call-to-action (CTA) such as 'Start Free Trial' or 'Request a Demo.' Following the hero, a features section uses concise copy and iconography to highlight the main benefits and differentiators of the SaaS offering. To build trust, a testimonials section presents quotes and avatars from real customers, while a logos bar displays recognizable client or partner brands. The pricing section transparently outlines available plans, features, and a secondary CTA, supporting conversion for both self-serve and sales-led models. An FAQ section addresses common objections, and a final CTA reinforces the conversion goal. The footer provides company details, navigation links, and social media. The design is fully responsive, accessible, and visually consistent with the SaaS brand. All UI primitives are sourced from shadcn/ui and styled via Tailwind CSS v4 tokens, ensuring seamless dark mode support and rapid iteration. The stack is Next.js 16 with React 19, using TanStack Query and Zustand for any interactive state (e.g., pricing toggle, FAQ expand/collapse), and Playwright/Vitest for testing. While the landing page is static and does not require backend APIs for content, the architecture is ready for future expansion (e.g., gated content, newsletter sign-up, or authentication). The page is optimized for SEO with semantic HTML, meta tags, and fast load times. Accessibility is a first-class concern: all interactive elements are keyboard-accessible, and color contrast meets WCAG standards. The codebase is production-grade, maintainable, and deployable to Vercel.

core: Hero section with value proposition and primary CTA
Features grid with icons and descriptions
Pricing plans with feature comparison and CTA
standard: SEO meta tags and OpenGraph support
Footer with navigation and social links

The design is fully responsive, accessible, and visually consistent with the SaaS brand. All UI primitives are sourced from shadcn/ui and styled via Tailwind CSS v4 tokens, ensuring seamless dark mode support and rapid iteration. The stack is Next.js 16 with React 19, using TanStack Query and Zustand for any interactive state (e.g., pricing toggle, FAQ expand/collapse), and Playwright/Vitest for testing. While the landing page is static and does not require backend APIs for content, the architecture is ready for future expansion (e.g., gated content, newsletter sign-up, or authentication). The page is optimized for SEO with semantic HTML, meta tags, and fast load times. Accessibility is a first-class concern: all interactive elements are keyboard-accessible, and color contrast meets WCAG standards. The codebase is production-grade, maintainable, and deployable to Vercel.
